questions.blocks: whether the next plan builds a new workbench slice or only keeps the repository shippable
questions.resolves_with: A product and priority call: no argument or test settles it. Prior art: Plan #6 says a same_capability verdict is a candidate for later design, and none was found (adjudication: 29 different_capability, 7 shared_shell).
questions.recommendation: Build nothing new here for now. Keep the workbench as the integration record and let Qualitative Coding finish its grounded-theory speed-run; open the next workbench slice only when a study needs exports from two producers together.
questions.default: Plan 007 (keep the repository shippable and its public page current) runs; no new workbench capability is built.
questions.evidence: Brian, 2026-11-06, answering this question: "on mixed mtheod work bench finsih that is not for a specific use case it is part of my broader vision". questions.short: Keeping deploy/ in step with the renderer

Deploys stay manual: the repository has no hosted CI (workspace rule) and the deploy is one command.

questions.question: Should the 1.0 benchmark include an hour of review by an outside qualitative or mixed-methods researcher, or is agreement with the corpus authors' own published coding enough for the 1.0 claim?
questions.blocks: the 1.0 benchmark's claim wording and whether S6 waits on a person
questions.resolves_with: A product call about what 1.0 promises: no test settles whether a person's review is required. Prior art: Qualitative Coding set the same bar for its finish (its step 5) and has not met it.
questions.recommendation: 1.0 claims only agreement with the authors' coding and the planted-failure results; an outside researcher's hour is the first post-1.0 step, so 1.0 does not wait on finding a person.
questions.default: The recommendation: the 1.0 claim is limited to agreement with the authors' coding.

questions.question: Which second rights-clear corpus, with its authors' own coding published, does S6 use?
questions.resolves_with: Prior art search (Zenodo, OSF, QDR open data, UK Data Service open access) under the S1 rules: open licence, participant consent to publication, the authors' coding published. No test needed.

questions.short: QC segment offsets against the Zenodo text
questions.question: Do the character offsets of QC's segments (and of the author's coded passages) point at the same text in the files downloaded from Zenodo, or did QC normalise the text on import?
questions.blocks: whether S1 can anchor every cited passage to the frozen source without a mapping step
questions.resolves_with: One check in S1: compare each segment's text with the frozen file at its offsets and count matches; a normalisation difference is mapped and the mapping recorded, never patched by hand.

questions.question: Which QC category becomes the S2 measurement instrument?
questions.resolves_with: Argument by a written rule, no test: the category with the most supporting passages that also has a matching author code, so a human reference exists. The roadmap's 2026-07-12 note gave this choice to Brian; under the 2026-11-05 authority rule (technical and method calls are the agent's) the agent decides and reports it, and Brian can overrule.

questions.question: Does S2 keep every condition of the repository's 2026-07-12 quantitative-strand brief (word-list count baseline, always-majority and TF-IDF baselines, the language model as a challenger, no embedding or topic output as the first measure, a feasibility readout before choosing the instrument, prevalence error because accuracy alone is prohibited, grouped splits with no turn-level intervals), and how are the cases a second model re-judges chosen?
questions.resolves_with: Argument, no test: the brief is the repository's own reviewed method decision and Plan #8 states no reason to drop any condition, so all are adopted (plan S2). The second model is removed from S2; if traces later show a gap, the cases it re-judges are chosen without the author's codes (for example where the language model and the regression disagree), so agreement with her coding is never inflated by giving only the misses a second chance.
questions.evidence: docs/plans/008_finish_workbench.md:109 and :121 now carry each condition; the brief's conditions are at docs/decisions/2026-07-12-first-quantitative-text-strand.md:18, :22 and :118.

questions.question: What unit does S2 label, and how do the author's coded passages (variable length, overlapping, exported from OpenQDA) map onto it?
questions.blocks: S2's denominator, its reference labels and its splits
questions.resolves_with: Argument from the data, no test: the unit is one interviewee turn as Qualitative Coding segmented it, so the qualitative and quantitative strands share one unit and every label opens a passage QC already anchors. A turn is a positive reference case when any author passage with the matching code overlaps it; passages that touch only interviewer turns are counted and listed. Counted on the frozen S1 files (study_workbench.py's anchoring): 630 interviewee turns of 1277 segments; of the author's 830 located passages, 717 lie within one interviewee turn, 75 span two or more and 38 touch only interviewer turns; 481 turns carry at least one author code. The interview is the independent group for splits, intervals and prevalence.
questions.evidence: Counts computed 2026-11-06 from examples/studies/open_science/qc/segments.json and the author's passages located by S1 (landing in the S1 pull request); plan S2 at docs/plans/008_finish_workbench.md:95.

questions.resolves_with: A product call about what his vision means: the repository's own map argues for it (one workbench-owned investigation spine; separate destinations named as the defect), but only Brian can say that map is the vision he meant.
questions.recommendation: Yes: each study is one investigation record built from its study definition, and S5 makes the PsychosisBank investigation one instance of it.
questions.default: The recommendation; Plan #8 proceeds with one investigation record per study.

questions.short: How the second corpus must differ
questions.question: On what must S6's second corpus differ from the first so that passing on it shows the workbench is general?
questions.blocks: S6 and the 'not for a specific use case' claim (acceptance A10)
questions.resolves_with: Argument, no test: a second set of interviews by the same team, on the same subject, coded in the same tool would show only that the code handles a near-copy. It must differ in subject, in research team and in coding tool or export format; if no published corpus meets all three, the benchmark page states which it shares and narrows the claim to match.
questions.evidence: Rule written into the plan, docs/plans/008_finish_workbench.md:53 and S6.
